Elaine H: Quick sync — noticing a PP bubble perf regression after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. 1F1B with microbatches=8 has ~12-18% tail latency increase on p3-like runners. Anyone else seeing this?
Raf: Yup, I saw the alert this morning. I pulled traces from the failing job (job id rjob-993). Will paste nvprof timeline in a sec.
Sanjay Patel: I ran a short repro on a 4-gpu PP topo. nvprof shows repeated all-reduce spikes at pipeline boundaries, ~3.0-3.5ms each. Timeline has compute -> gap -> allreduce -> compute. Gap aligns with kvcache eviction bursts in logs.
Marisa G: Did the kernel selector change the attention/matmul kernel variants? I remember the rollout switched small-seq to fused-int8 matmul to speed up tokens <512.
Raf: Correct — the selector now prefers fused_matmul_int8 for seq<512. That path is faster for single-node but seems to introduce extra small synchronizations when combined with our PP rendezvous.
Sanjay Patel: Snippet from nvprof (trimmed):
```
AllReduce: avg 3.2ms  p50 2.9ms  p95 4.1ms
MatMul_fused_int8: avg 1.05ms
MatMul_fp16: avg 0.72ms
Idle gaps between kernels: ~1.1-1.4ms
```
Raf: Timeline screenshot shows CPU-side enqueue of allreduce happens slightly late because fused kernel returns faster but doesn't populate the expected NVTX window we use for overlap heuristics. So the overlap logic thinks compute finished later and delays comm kickoff.
Marisa G: That makes sense — our comm/compute overlap relies on NVTX markers and kernel duration heuristics. If selector changes shape/timing, the overlap heuristic misfires.
Elaine H: Practical questions: 1) Can we revert selector rollout quickly? 2) Short-term microbatch sweep to see if different microbatch counts hide the regression? 3) Add a fallback in selector to emit NVTX span for fused kernels?
Raf: For (1) I can toggle the selector flag for the hosted pool — it's feature-flagged. Quick revert should be safe.
Sanjay Patel: I ran a manual sweep: microbatches=4 reduced p95 tail by ~6% (but throughput dropped ~5%). microbatches=2 removes most tail but throughput hit ~12% lower. So tradeoff.
Marisa G: For (3) I can change the fused kernel wrapper to emit NVTX begin/end around the heavy compute region so our overlap heuristics see it as before. That should avoid the delay without reverting. I'll prototype and run a gold test.
Raf: Also noticed KV cache churn: when fused path returns early we get more KV eviction windows (shorter per-step time), causing kvcache eviction to run more frequently — might amplify all-reduce contention. Adding a small grace window before eviction lowered spikes in a quick run.
Elaine H: Action items: Raf -> flip selector flag for the hot pool and rerun regression check (ETA 30m). Marisa -> prototype NVTX spans for fused kernels and run 1F1B microbatch sweep across [2,4,8,16] on staging (ETA EOD). Sanjay -> add a kvcache stress test to reproduce eviction alignment (ETA EOD). We'll reconvene after runs.

Raf: Flip done for pool=prod-hosted, kicked off regression job rjob-1002. Initial numbers look promising (p95 back down to baseline). Will post full numbers when job finishes.
Marisa G: Prototype NVTX change compiled and unit tests green. Running 1F1B sweep now.
Sanjay Patel: kvcache stress harness added to ci/perf (cc @marisa). Trying local reproducer now.
Elaine H: Awesome. If the NVTX patch fixes overlap without throughput loss, we can ship it and keep selector enabled. If not, we'll keep selector off and iterate. Thanks all :eyes:
